meals.strInstructions:
STEP 1
Heat the oil in a karahi or wok on high heat. Add the chicken and fry for 5-7 minutes until it changes colour.
STEP 2
Add the ginger garlic paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until the raw smell goes.
STEP 3
Add the chopped tomatoes, cover and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until soft. Remove any loose tomato skins if you like.
STEP 4
Add the salt, red chilli powder, crushed red chilli, turmeric, cumin and black pepper. Fry (bhuna) on high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring, until the oil separates.
STEP 5
Lower the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt and cook for 3-4 minutes until the chicken is tender.
STEP 6
Add the green chillies, ginger julienne and garam masala. Cook for 2 more minutes.
STEP 7
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or roti.

STEP 1
Heat the ghee in a large heavy pot. Fry the sliced onion until golden brown, then remove it and keep it aside for garnish.
STEP 2
In the same ghee, add the beef and ginger garlic paste. Fry for about 5 minutes until the meat changes colour.
STEP 3
Add the salt, red chilli powder, turmeric and nihari masala. Fry for 2-3 minutes.
STEP 4
Add 6 cups of water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 4-6 hours (or pressure cook for 45-60 minutes) until the meat is very tender.
STEP 5
Mix the wheat flour with 1 cup of water until smooth. Slowly pour it into the pot while stirring, so no lumps form.
STEP 6
Cook on low heat for 20-30 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy is thick and silky. Add a little hot water if it gets too thick.
STEP 7
Serve hot, topped with the fried onion, ginger julienne, green chillies, coriander and a squeeze of lemon. Eat with naan.

STEP 1
Soak the wheat and barley overnight. Soak the lentils and rice for 2 hours.
STEP 2
Drain, then boil the grains and lentils in 6 cups of water with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 1 1/2 - 2 hours until very soft. Mash or blend them coarsely.
STEP 3
Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the sliced onions until golden brown. Remove half of the onions and keep them for garnish.
STEP 4
Add the beef and ginger garlic paste to the pot with the remaining onions and fry for 5 minutes. Add the rest of the salt and turmeric, the red chilli powder and coriander powder, and fry for 2 more minutes.
STEP 5
Add 3 cups of water, cover and cook on low heat for 1 1/2 - 2 hours (or pressure cook for 30-40 minutes) until the meat is very tender.
STEP 6
Shred the meat finely with a wooden spoon or a few quick pulses in a chopper.
STEP 7
Add the mashed grain mixture to the meat. Cook on low heat for 30-45 minutes, stirring and beating well, until thick and stringy. Add hot water if it gets too thick. Stir in the garam masala.
STEP 8
Serve topped with fried onions, ginger julienne, green chillies, mint, lemon and a pinch of chaat masala. Eat with naan.

STEP 1
Wash the rice and soak it in water for 30 minutes.
STEP 2
Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the sliced onions until golden brown. Remove half of the onions and keep them for layering.
STEP 3
Add the chicken and ginger garlic paste to the pot and fry for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, biryani masala, red chilli powder, turmeric and 2 tsp salt. Cook until the tomatoes are soft and the oil separates.
STEP 4
Stir in the yogurt and dried plums. Cover and cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy is thick.
STEP 5
Boil a large pot of water with 2 tbsp salt and the whole spices. Add the drained rice and boil for 5-7 minutes until about three-quarters cooked. Drain well.
STEP 6
In the pot with the chicken, spread half of the rice over the chicken. Add the mint, coriander, green chillies, fried onions and lemon slices, then the rest of the rice. Sprinkle the saffron milk (or food colour) and kewra water on top.
STEP 7
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat (dum) for 10-15 minutes, ideally with a flat pan (tawa) under the pot.
STEP 8
Mix gently from the sides and serve hot with raita and salad.
meals.strMeasure11: 2 tsp + 2 tbsp for the rice water
meals.strMeasure12: 2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 4 green cardamoms
meals.strIngredient18: Saffron soaked in warm milk (or a pinch of yellow food colour)

meals.strInstructions:
STEP 1
Chop the onion very finely and squeeze out all its water with your hands or a cloth.
STEP 2
Put the mince and all the other ingredients (except the oil) in a bowl. Mix and knead for 3-4 minutes, or pulse in a chopper, until the mixture is sticky.
STEP 3
Cover and rest the mixture in the fridge for 30-60 minutes.
STEP 4
With wet hands, press portions of the mixture evenly around flat skewers, about 2 cm thick.
STEP 5
Cook over hot coals, under a grill or in an oven at 220°C for 12-15 minutes, turning and brushing with oil, until browned and cooked through.
STEP 6
Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings, lemon and naan.

STEP 1
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the sliced onions until golden brown.
STEP 2
Add the mutton and ginger garlic paste. Fry for about 5 minutes until the meat changes colour.
STEP 3
Add the tomatoes, salt, red chilli powder, turmeric and coriander powder. Cook (bhuna) for 8-10 minutes until the tomatoes break down and the oil separates.
STEP 4
Stir in the yogurt and cook for 3 minutes. Add 3 cups of water, cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes (or pressure cook for 20 minutes) until the meat is almost tender.
STEP 5
Add the potatoes and 1 more cup of water. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the gravy is as thick as you like.
STEP 6
Stir in the garam masala, add the green chillies and coriander, and serve hot with roti or rice.

STEP 1
Wash the rice and soak it for 30 minutes. Wash the masoor daal until the water runs clear.
STEP 2
For the daal: boil the daal in 4 cups of water with the turmeric, red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, ginger garlic paste and tomato. Cook on medium heat for 20-25 minutes until soft, then whisk until smooth.
STEP 3
For the rice: bring 3 cups of water with 1 tsp salt to a boil. Add the drained rice and cook on high heat until most of the water is absorbed. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10-12 minutes.
STEP 4
For the tarka: heat the ghee in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds and sliced garlic and fry until the garlic is light golden. Add the dried red chillies and curry leaves for a few seconds.
STEP 5
Pour the hot tarka over the daal and garnish with coriander and green chillies.
STEP 6
Serve the daal over the rice with kachumar salad and achar.
meals.strMeasure5: 1 tsp for daal + 1 tsp for rice

meals.strInstructions:
STEP 1
Chop the onion finely and squeeze out its water. Deseed and finely chop one tomato.
STEP 2
In a large bowl, mix the mince with all the other ingredients except the tomato slices and the frying fat. Knead well for 2-3 minutes.
STEP 3
Cover and rest the mixture in the fridge for 30 minutes.
STEP 4
With wet hands, shape the mixture into large flat round patties, about 1 cm thick and 10 cm wide. Press a thin tomato slice into the top of each one.
STEP 5
Heat the fat in a large flat pan on medium-high heat. Shallow-fry the kababs for 3-4 minutes on each side until crisp, dark brown and cooked through.
STEP 6
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with naan, raita and green chutney.
meals.strIngredient8: Maize flour (makai ka atta) or gram flour
meals.strIngredient15: Beef fat, ghee or oil (for shallow frying)

meals.strInstructions:
STEP 1
Wash the rice, soak it for 30 minutes, then drain and crush it lightly with your hands or a rolling pin.
STEP 2
Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot.
STEP 3
Add the rice and cardamom. Simmer on low heat for 40-50 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the rice is very soft and the milk has thickened.
STEP 4
Add the sugar and cook for another 5-10 minutes, stirring.
STEP 5
Turn off the heat and stir in most of the almonds and pistachios and the kewra water.
STEP 6
Let it cool, then chill in the fridge. Serve garnished with the remaining nuts.

STEP 1
For the syrup: boil the sugar, water and cardamoms for 5-7 minutes until slightly sticky. Add the rose water and keep the syrup warm.
STEP 2
For the dough: mix the milk powder, flour, baking powder and cardamom powder. Rub in the ghee.
STEP 3
Add the warm milk a little at a time and mix gently into a soft, smooth dough. Do not knead hard. Rest it for 5-10 minutes.
STEP 4
With greased hands, roll the dough into 16-18 small balls with no cracks.
STEP 5
Heat the oil on low to medium heat. Fry the balls slowly for 6-8 minutes, gently moving the oil around them, until deep golden brown all over. If the oil is too hot, they will brown outside but stay raw inside.
STEP 6
Drain the jamuns and put them straight into the warm syrup.
STEP 7
Let them soak for at least 1-2 hours until they swell. Serve warm or at room temperature.
